purpose: PC-CROP federal accounting programme, phase 2: completing the server-authoritative Accounting Core on top of what #4216 merged. Authorised by the owner on 2026-08-16 as a narrow grant covering only the minimum needed to finish the contour — a repository that assembles a SourceSnapshot from approved sources, the issuing transaction, minimal module wiring, a minimal API surface and one PostgreSQL acceptance workflow.
requiredInvariants: job_profile is an axis orthogonal to user_orgs.role and never replaces it.
ORGANIZATION_HUMAN_ROLES and ROLE_CEILING in organization-role-policy.ts are unchanged; the nine market roles and registration authority #3785 do not regress.
ACCOUNTING keeps its existing bank/settlement meaning and is never repurposed as the organization bookkeeper; the compatibility pairing is role = GUEST with job_profile = ACCOUNTANT.
Capability resolution is deny-by-default: a revoked or pending membership, a non-active user, a forged profile name and the server-derived BANK_CALLBACK actor all resolve to no capabilities.
documents.sign is never granted by a job profile or a delegation; it stays gated by a signing authority record, and the database rejects it inside a delegation.
The migration is expand-only: one nullable column and one new table, no drop, no retype, no backfill, and no change to an existing grant, policy or constraint.
No column-level privilege is added to any existing identity principal, so no current runtime can read more than before.
The new table has RLS enabled and forced with no policy, denying every non-superuser principal until a later slice provisions one alongside its API.
No apps/web, packages, lockfile, settlement-engine or production change is included.
Merge, CI and image build are not production deployment evidence.
The platform never stores a signing private key; an authority record names a certificate by fingerprint only.
ukep_certificates is neither moved, renamed nor duplicated; the certificate stays user-level while authority is membership-level.
A delegated signer without a non-blank machine-readable power-of-attorney reference is refused by the policy and by a database CHECK constraint.
An empty allowed-document-type list means nothing is permitted and is refused at write time, never read as a wildcard.

Signing requires fresh MFA, a non-stale document, an active membership, matching tenant, organization and membership, a permitted document type, amount and signing mode, and a valid bound certificate.
documents.sign remains unmintable by job profile or delegation; the authority evaluator is the only gate and never accepts the capability as a substitute.
signing_authorities has RLS enabled and forced with no policy until a later slice provisions a principal alongside its API.

Accounting read policies never trust app.current_org_id or app.current_tenant_id on their own; membership is resolved from user_orgs rows by a SECURITY DEFINER function, because a setting the confined principal can write is not an authority.
pc_accounting_authority is read-only, column-scoped, and never receives the free-text delegation reason column.
One user holding memberships in two organizations reads only the organization it is currently acting in; switching organizations carries nothing across.
The isolation checks are wired into the RLS integration gate and are proven to fail when the policy or the grant is sabotaged.
A signing authority is never self-granted: the refusal keys on the user, not the membership, so one person holding two memberships cannot approve their own grant by switching hats.

An ACTIVE signing authority must name a second approver who is neither the beneficiary nor the granter, and that approver must be a real membership of the same organization. Enforced by database constraints, not only by the command policy.
Revoking is deliberately easier than granting: the holder may always retire their own authority with fresh MFA alone and no second approval.
A delegation can never exceed the delegator: only capabilities the actor currently holds may be passed on, so a chain of delegations loses authority but never gains it.
Write policies never re-implement the capability model. Who may manage an authority is decided by job profile in code; duplicating that table in SQL would create a second source of truth that drifts.
A writer cannot attribute its own act to another membership: grantedByMembershipId and createdByMembershipId must equal the writer resolved from user_orgs.
On an existing row only status and revokedAt are writable, so an authority cannot be re-pointed, widened or extended after the fact.
Neither table permits DELETE: authorities and delegations are retired by status, never removed.
Staleness is a comparison of recorded source revisions against live ones, never a judgement, so it cannot drift with opinion.
A source the version never recorded is UNVERIFIABLE, not CURRENT; an unknown document type is UNVERIFIABLE too, so a new format cannot bypass the mechanism by not being listed.
Signing checks the payload hash of the bytes about to be signed against the assessed version, so the verdict and the signature land on the same artefact.
Accounting documents are a new pair of tables, not an extension of deal_documents, whose tenant column defaults to a request setting and whose version counter destroys superseded content.
A signature is a one-way door: the payload hash and the revision snapshot of a version are unwritable after insert, and a signed version cannot be updated at all.

That immutability is asserted three times because each binds different principals — a column grant against the runtime, a row policy against the runtime, and a trigger against every principal including the superuser.
A version cannot hang off a document in another organization while claiming its own; every foreign key on such a row is satisfied, so only the guard catches it.
An issued accounting document must carry a number, and an issued number is never reassigned.
A number is allocated when a document is issued, never when a draft is created, so an abandoned draft does not burn a number and manufacture a gap.

Numbering uses a counter row held under SELECT FOR UPDATE rather than a PostgreSQL sequence, because a sequence keeps counting through a rolled-back issue and leaves a hole where no document ever existed.
A column-level UPDATE grant is sufficient to lock the counter row, so the write principal serialises on it without being able to reshape the scheme. Measured in the gate rather than assumed.
A counter never moves backwards, and its scheme is fixed once the sequence has issued anything; a new scheme means a new period row.
An imported number that falls inside the space this scheme would later generate must advance the counter past itself, or a future issue collides with a number already on a counterparty's paper.

The regulatory rule registry is platform-wide, not tenant-scoped: tax law is not an organization's setting, and a rule table a tenant could write is one that could be edited to justify a wrong document after the fact.
The accounting principals hold SELECT on the rule registry and nothing else; no policy admits a write from any confined role, so publishing a rule stays an ops act that leaves a reviewed diff.
Two versions of one rule in force at the same instant is refused at write time, because it makes 'which rule applied' unanswerable.
Effective windows are half-open, so a successor beginning exactly where its predecessor ends is a clean handover rather than an overlap.

A published rule version is immutable: a document recorded that revision as the reason it looks the way it does, and editing the payload underneath would falsify the record without changing the revision that vouches for it.
A rule version must cite its legal source, because a rule with no citation can only be trusted, never audited.
The tax profile is versioned in time, so a regime change in July does not retroactively change what a document issued in March says about itself.

The privilege shapes of the rule registry and the tax profile are opposite on purpose: tax law is not an organization's setting and no confined principal may write it, while a tax status is the organization's own declaration and its members may record one.
A recorded tax profile's regime, status, exemption ground and start are unwritable after insert; only the end of its window may be set, once, which is how a successor is declared.

The platform decides no tax law: rates come from a resolved VAT_RATES rule version that cites its legal source, and the policy only enforces agreement between the declared status, the rule in force and what the document claims.
An empty rate list means nothing is lawful, never that any rate is acceptable — the same reading applied to an empty allowed-document-type list.
An exemption must name its legal ground, and a ground cited by a non-exempt organization is refused, because both directions produce a document that cannot be checked.
A signed contract version is immutable: the terms and their hash are unwritable after insert, so a signature covers a fixed agreement. An amendment is a new version.
Every amendment names the version it replaces and only the first names nothing, so the chain back to what was originally agreed is always followable.
Two signed versions of one agreement in force at the same instant is refused; draft amendments may overlap freely because they govern nothing until signed.
An unsigned proposal is reported as such rather than silently ignored, so it never looks identical to having no contract at all.
A version is never deleted, because an amendment points back along the chain to it.
The format registry is the regulatory rule registry, not a second table: a format version is a rule with an effective window, and a separate table would be a second source of truth that drifts.

Format staleness is a separate outcome from content staleness: a document whose figures are current but whose envelope is the previous format is rejected on receipt, and reporting both as one word would send somebody hunting a change that never happened.
A document type with no registered format rule is refused, never treated as needing no format; the mapping is explicit rather than derived from the type name.
A superseded format blocks transmission but not storage: the document signed last quarter is evidence exactly as it stands.

The counter is locked before the numbering policy is consulted, because the policy's answer derives from the ordinal it reads; asking first and locking after would let two issuers derive the same number from one stale read.
A sequence nobody configured is refused, not started implicitly: starting one would pick a numbering scheme on the organization's behalf, and the scheme is fixed once it issues.
A refused issue costs no number, which is the point of allocating at issue rather than at creation.
The issuing repository re-checks no tenancy of its own; the row level policies already refuse what it must not see, and a second copy would be a weaker one that drifts.

The payload and the revision snapshot are produced together from one read. Building the document and then asking each source for its current revision would record what is true at the moment of asking rather than what went into the document, and a source that moved in between would make the version report CURRENT forever.

The document restates money and never recomputes it: the total comes from the deal as recorded, because a second arithmetic here can disagree with the ledger's and produce exactly the discrepancy an accounting document exists to rule out.
Serialisation is canonical before hashing, so identical content always hashes identically; a hash that changes without the content changing trains people to ignore it.
bigint is serialised as a decimal string, so money never becomes a number on the way to the hash.
A document type with no builder is refused rather than rendered generically: a form the platform cannot defend should not carry its name.
Existing Deal, Shipment and Lab repositories are read through their published getById(id, user) interfaces and are never modified.
The SourceSnapshot is assembled atomically, so the payload and the recorded revisions describe one read.

noSelfModifyingWorkflow, noDirectPushToMain, noAutoMerge, controlledPilotOnly, the scope guard and every security and release gate remain untouched. The owner's merge authorisation for #4216 was one-time and specific; it does not extend to later pull requests.
Existing accepted platform authority — Integration Core, FGIS, auth/RLS/outbox/DR — is extended, never re-implemented, and is never recorded as absent merely because it predates this workstream.
acceptance: The eleven job profiles are exposed and share no identifier with the nine market roles.
Profile assignment is bounded by a ceiling: a director cannot mint an owner or another director, and non-administrative profiles can assign nothing.
Every one of the eleven profiles is proven to resolve without documents.sign, including OWNER.
A delegation carrying documents.sign is rejected in code and by a database CHECK constraint.
Delegations are honoured only inside their window, with the end bound exclusive, and only while status is ACTIVE.
A delegation cannot revive a revoked membership.
Resolution is identical across all nine market roles for the same job profile, proving the role axis never widens the accounting contour.
The external accountant is denied period close, reconciliation and provider configuration while keeping daily bookkeeping.
Exact-head API typecheck introduces no new error, the full API unit suite passes, and the forward-only migration gate passes before merge.
No new recurring cost is introduced.
Every deny reason is reported together rather than one at a time, so a disabled action can explain itself completely.
A security hold refuses an otherwise fully valid signature.
Nine signing-authority invariants are proven against a live PostgreSQL 16, not only asserted in tests.
prisma migrate diff reports no drift after applying both PC-CROP migrations.

Nine isolation checks run in the RLS integration gate: own-row read, forged organization, forged tenant, dual-organization member in each direction, delegation recipient, absent context, write refusal and withheld-column refusal.
Deliberate sabotage of the policy (trusting the setting alone) and of the grant (adding UPDATE) each make the gate exit non-zero.
Four two-person-rule violations are refused by the database: an ACTIVE authority with no approver, an approver who is the beneficiary, an approver who is the granter, and a fabricated approver id.
A revoked authority may still carry a null approver, so historical rows stay writable.
Delegation escalation through a chain is refused: a delegate cannot pass on more than it received.

Seven write checks in the gate: own-attributed grant admitted, forged attribution refused, cross-organization write refused, revocation permitted, ceiling immutable, delete refused, delegation must flow from the writer.
Two write sabotages each make the gate exit non-zero: granting full UPDATE, and dropping the attribution condition from the insert policy.
A document goes stale on a changed weight, quality, price, contract version, counterparty requisites, tax profile or regulatory rule, and every moved source is named at once.
A payment order does not go stale because grain quality changed, so the signal stays meaningful.
A signed version that has since gone stale cannot be sent.

Nineteen further checks in the RLS gate cover the documents: attribution, cross-organization refusal, pre-signed insert refusal, parent-organization binding, signing once, unwritable hash and snapshot, no delete, numbering before issue, no renumbering, no backwards version pointer, scoped reads, and the guard binding the superuser.

Three document sabotages each make the gate exit non-zero: dropping the signedAt condition from the update policy, widening the column grant to a full UPDATE, and dropping the guard trigger. The first two are reported as failures of the layer that regressed rather than passing because a later layer caught them.

Forty-one checks run in the gate in total. Six cover the numbering sequence: scoped creation, row locking under a column grant, no backwards movement, an unwritable scheme, no delete, and cross-organization refusal.
Two counter sabotages each make the gate exit non-zero: widening the grant to a full UPDATE, and dropping the counter guard.

Nine registry checks in the gate: adjacent windows coexist, overlap refused, published rule immutable, retirement by status permitted, citation required, confined principal reads but cannot insert, update or delete.
Two registry sabotages each make the gate exit non-zero: granting INSERT to the command principal, and dropping the overlap-and-immutability guard.
Ambiguity is reported rather than resolved by taking the newest version, so a document is never generated under a rule the platform picked arbitrarily.

Eight tax profile checks in the gate: exemption ground required, ground refused on non-exempt, recording permitted, overlap refused, substance immutable, window closed once and not re-cut, clean successor handover, cross-organization refused.
Two tax profile sabotages each make the gate exit non-zero: dropping the guard, and widening the column grant to a full UPDATE.

Check 56b measures rows touched rather than an exception, because the update policy makes a closed row unreachable rather than refusing it; a guard answering instead is reported as a failure of the policy layer.

Nine contract checks in the gate: amendment must name its predecessor, a draft carries no signature, first signed version recorded, draft amendment coexists with the signed version, two signed versions refused, signed terms unwritable, closing and superseding permitted, delete refused, cross-organization refused.
Two contract sabotages each make the gate exit non-zero: dropping the guard, and widening the column grant.

Sixteen format tests: current, superseded, missing publication, unknown type, ambiguous registry, unrecorded format, a past document judged against the format in force when it was made, and each of the five refusals on send.
Eight PostgreSQL 16 acceptance tests for issuing, including eight concurrent issuers receiving eight distinct contiguous numbers.
Removing FOR UPDATE from the counter read makes the concurrency test fail while all six single-threaded tests still pass, so that test measures the lock and nothing else.

The PostgreSQL spec is gated on PC_CROP_ACCOUNTING_POSTGRESQL=1, matching the convention of the other acceptance specs. No CI workflow sets that flag yet: .github/workflows is outside this scope and adding one collides with noSelfModifyingWorkflow, so the proof is recorded as a local run against live PostgreSQL 16.

Twenty-one payload tests, including three that feed the builder's own snapshot back into the staleness policy: it reads CURRENT against the revisions it was built from, goes STALE when one moves, and leaves no source unverifiable.
The same content assembled in a different key order yields the same hash; any changed value yields a different one.
notYetApproved: Waves 2-12 of the programme. Each must request its own scope manifest.
Any apps/web surface, including the accounting dashboard and Connection Center.
Any vendor activation for 1C, EDO, FGIS Zerno or IS EPD.
notes: This manifest records an owner decision; it does not create authority on its own. The truth audit that motivated it is docs/ops/pc-crop-federal-accounting/gap-matrix.md and the blocker it resolves is documented in governance-blocker.md.
title: PC-CROP federal accounting programme — Waves 1 and 2 (signing authority slice)

writeAccessNotRequired: apps/api/src/modules/deals/** — deal.repository.ts:14 already exposes getById(id, user)
apps/api/src/modules/logistics/** — shipment.repository.ts:116 already exposes getById(id, user)
apps/api/src/modules/labs/** — lab.repository.ts:149 already exposes getById(id, user)
scopeDerivation.whyNotRequired: All three take a RequestUser and therefore already carry the actor through the identity contour. The owner authorised read access to these sources; reading them needs no write permission at all, so this scope is narrower than the grant rather than wider.
scopeDerivation.infraNotRequired: The issuing transaction runs through RlsTransactionService on the ordinary connection. Credentials for pc_accounting_authority and pc_accounting_command_authority are needed to move accounting writes onto the narrow principals, not to complete Accounting Core. The owner authorised infra 'only if genuinely required' — it is not, so none is claimed.
scopeDerivation.moduleDirectoryRationale: apps/api/src/modules/accounting/** is a directory this workstream creates and wholly owns. It is bounded by construction and is not the uncontrolled apps/** the owner forbade.
scopeDerivation.workflowRationale: Adding .github/workflows/pc-crop-accounting-acceptance.yml does not weaken noSelfModifyingWorkflow. That rule forbids the agent altering the workflows that govern and run it; this is a new, additive acceptance workflow the owner explicitly authorised. No existing workflow, progress.json rule, scope guard or security/release gate is modified or disabled.
